title: María Félix's birth chart
metaDescription: María Félix's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 13.5° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mercury and Pluto sit 0.0° from an exact sextile — near enough that the tradition reads thinking and depth as a single working part. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Taurus, but precisely: 13.5°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Mercury in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Venus at 3.9° Gemini, Mars at 1.5° Leo. Venus in a air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a fire sign reads as drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mercury and Pluto: 0.0° from an exact sextile. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, Mercury square Mars at 1.9°, and the Sun square Uranus at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: None of the seven classical planets falls in a sign the old scheme marks as strong or stretched. Worth saying plainly rather than leaving out: there is no ready-made verdict from the dignity table here, and the chart’s weight sits in its angles instead.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 5 in air, 1 in earth, 1 in fire, 1 in water by element, 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 1 cardinal by modality. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible. Mercury crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day, so its sign is left open. Nothing here ran retrograde — all ten in direct motion that day.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Leo into Virgo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.0° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
